findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left Hoover sign, drift without pronation, dragging gait and entraining tremor; hemisensory loss supportive only
action_criteria.label: Examine for positive functional signs
action_criteria.rationale: The left-sided weakness and tremor are diagnosed at the bedside: Hoover sign, drift without pronation, dragging gait and tremor entrainment are signs of clinical incompatibility (DSM-5 criterion B; Daum 2014).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No acute infarct on DWI and no other lesion to explain the left-sided deficit
action_criteria.label: Non-contrast brain MRI, once
action_criteria.rationale: Left hemiparesis evolving over 24 hours in a woman with migraine, who herself raised a migraine-related stroke, is triaged as a possible stroke; one non-contrast MRI with DWI answers that question, and gadolinium adds nothing (Espay 2018).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm with normal conduction and QT interval
action_criteria.label: 12-lead ECG
action_criteria.rationale: Episodes of apparent unresponsiveness: NICE advises a 12-lead ECG after transient loss of consciousness (CG109) and after a suspected seizure (NG217). The event semiology already favours functional seizures, so it does not contribute to the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Habitual events recorded on video with no EEG change and a normal interictal record
action_criteria.label: Video-EEG to capture a habitual event
action_criteria.rationale: Staring spells with unresponsiveness can be focal impaired-awareness seizures; eyelid fluttering and immediate recovery support functional seizures but no single feature is diagnostic, so the ILAE documented level rests on a habitual event recorded without ictal change (LaFrance 2013; Avbersek 2010; AAN 2025). Without the recording, the positive signs and the semiology of witnessed events support the diagnosis at a lower ILAE level of certainty (LaFrance 2013).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serotonergic pairing of the SSRI and the triptan, managed by counselling
action_criteria.label: Review the medication list
action_criteria.rationale: Fluoxetine with sumatriptan is a serotonergic pair worth counselling on, but it does not change the diagnosis or the plan; no benzodiazepine or antiseizure drug is prescribed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Quantifies mood, anxiety and symptom burden to guide therapy; does not make the diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Neuropsychological assessment of the comorbidity
action_criteria.rationale: Depression and post-traumatic stress symptoms are treatment targets; a battery can quantify them but does not make the diagnosis (Espay 2018).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on positive signs and treatment trials in FND
action_criteria.label: Search the literature on FND diagnosis and treatment
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; the diagnosis and the plan rest on this patient's examination and recorded data, not on a search.

prohibited_recommendations: Order further investigations once the positive diagnosis is established, without a new specific clinical question (repeat MRI, CT, lumbar puncture, EMG or nerve conduction studies, evoked potentials, PET).
Tell the patient the symptoms are imagined, feigned, 'all in your head', or that nothing is wrong.
Perform invasive testing without a specific indication (lumbar puncture, nerve or muscle biopsy, catheter angiography).
Start or escalate antiseizure medication for the functional seizures.
Give benzodiazepines or intubate for a typical functional seizure.
Give gadolinium contrast without a specific indication.
required_recommendations: Make a positive diagnosis of functional neurological disorder (mixed: functional seizures with functional left-sided weakness and tremor) based on the left Hoover sign, drift without pronation, dragging monoplegic gait and tremor entrainment and the semiology of the habitual staring events, confirmed on video-EEG where recorded, and not by exclusion of other disease.

Explain the diagnosis to the patient, and with consent to the family, as a common and genuine disorder of nervous system functioning that can improve, show the positive signs, and give written information.
Refer for physiotherapy with expertise in functional motor disorder (motor retraining, Nielsen 2015 consensus).

Refer for psychological therapy by a clinician experienced in FND (CBT-informed) and treat the comorbid post-traumatic stress disorder and depression, with a trauma-informed approach given the adolescent sexual abuse.

Give the patient, family and ward a written plan for typical events: keep safe, do not restrain, wait for the event to end, and do not give emergency benzodiazepines or intubate for a typical functional seizure.

avoided_actions.rationale: With positive functional signs and no infarct on MRI there is no embolic source to look for.
The events are staring spells without collapse or pallor; rhythm monitoring answers no question here.
The deficit evolved over 24 hours with no thrombolysis decision pending; the single MRI with DWI answers the stroke question and a CT adds radiation without adding information.
No fever, headache, meningism or encephalopathy; a lumbar puncture is invasive and answers no question.
PET has no role in functional weakness or functional seizures.
Hemiparesis with normal reflexes and positive functional signs is not a neuromuscular question; a normal study reinforces the search for an organic cause.
A hemisensory loss that follows no anatomical distribution is not a somatosensory pathway question; evoked potentials add nothing.

accepted: Functional neurological disorder — functional left hemisensorimotor syndrome and PNES, with comorbid PTSD

differential.key_features: Staring with unresponsiveness raises focal seizures, but eyelid fluttering and immediate recovery without confusion favour functional seizures. Habitual events recorded on video-EEG without ictal change; co-occurring epilepsy remains possible in about one in five patients with functional seizures.

differential.diagnosis: Hemiplegic migraine or prolonged migraine aura
differential.key_features: She has migraine and feared a prolonged aura, but her migraine is without aura, there is no headache phase, the weakness carries positive functional signs and the MRI is normal.

differential.diagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack
differential.key_features: Left hemiparesis over 24 hours in a migraineur raises stroke; Hoover sign, drift without pronation, normal reflexes and an MRI without restricted diffusion argue against it.
A prior unexplained episode of right leg weakness raises demyelination, but the current signs are incompatible with a central lesion and the MRI shows no white matter lesion.

key_clinical_evidence: Positive signs of functional weakness and tremor on the left: Hoover sign, drift without pronation of the arm, dragging monoplegic gait and tremor entrainment; the non-anatomical hemisensory loss and normal walking when unobserved are supportive only.
The staring spells with eyelid fluttering and immediate recovery without confusion have features typical of functional seizures, but semiology alone does not exclude focal seizures.
Video-EEG recorded one habitual staring event with eyelid flutter and no EEG change, with a normal interictal record.
A single non-contrast MRI with DWI, indicated by the stroke question in a migraineur, shows no infarct or other lesion.

Post-traumatic stress symptoms after witnessing a coworker's injury, the anniversary of adolescent abuse and depression are context and treatment targets; they are neither required nor sufficient for the diagnosis.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A remote family history of self-limited childhood epilepsy does not make her events epileptic; the semiology decides, and a habitual event recorded without ictal EEG change confirms it.
red_herrings.data_point: Maternal aunt with childhood epilepsy that resolved
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchoring on an epileptic cause and starting antiseizure medication before an event is recorded

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Her migraine is without aura and there is no headache phase; the positive signs and one normal MRI answer the question.
red_herrings.data_point: Migraine, and her own concern about a prolonged aura or migraine-related stroke
red_herrings.intended_effect: Labelling the deficit hemiplegic migraine, or ordering repeated vascular imaging

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Psychiatric comorbidity neither establishes nor refutes FND; it is a treatment target.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchoring on a 'psychosomatic' label without eliciting positive signs, or dismissing the symptoms

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Trauma is common in FND but neither necessary nor sufficient; the positive signs and the event semiology make the diagnosis, and the post-traumatic symptoms need treatment.
red_herrings.data_point: Witnessed a coworker's traumatic injury 6 weeks ago, and the anniversary of adolescent sexual abuse
red_herrings.intended_effect: Treating trauma as proof of FND and skipping the examination and the event recording

sequence_constraints.reason: The examination comes first: its positive signs decide whether imaging has a specific question to answer (Espay 2018).

findings.result: Left hip extension weak on direct testing, full strength during contralateral right hip flexion against resistance.
Left arm drifts down with eyes closed without pronation of the forearm.
Left hand tremor takes up the frequency of the rhythm she copies with the right hand, or stops during the task.
Left leg dragged behind with the foot kept on the floor.
Left hemisensory loss including the face that follows no nerve or root distribution; normal walking when unaware of being observed; not counted as rule-in signs.
Reflexes 2+ and symmetric; no pathological reflexes.

clinical_assessment.impression: Positive signs of functional weakness and tremor: left Hoover sign, drift without pronation of the left arm, dragging monoplegic gait and left hand tremor entrainment. The pattern is inconsistent with a structural lesion. No event was observed during the examination.

interactions: Fluoxetine with sumatriptan: additive serotonergic effect; serotonin syndrome is rare with this combination but reported; counsel on agitation, tremor, sweating and hyperthermia and keep triptan use within the labelled maximum.
general.proposed: Sumatriptan 100 mg as needed for migraine, max 2 doses/day; Fluoxetine 20 mg once daily
general.summary: One serotonergic interaction (fluoxetine with sumatriptan) that needs counselling rather than a change of drug.
warnings: Sumatriptan: contraindicated in hemiplegic or basilar migraine and in ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack.
Sulfonamide antibiotic allergy (rash): sumatriptan contains a sulfonamide group; cross-reactivity is not expected and the drug is already tolerated.

artifacts.description: Eyelid flutter artifact in Fp1/Fp2 during the event

background.description: Symmetric 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, reactive to eye opening. Normal sleep architecture.
background.recording: 24-hour inpatient video-EEG, wake and sleep, 10-20 electrode placement

findings.morphology: Day 1, 11:05, duration 1 min 40 s: motionless staring with rapid eyelid fluttering, no response to questions, immediate return to normal conversation afterwards; the patient identified it as one of her usual spells. Posterior dominant rhythm present throughout the event, with eyelid flutter artifact over the frontal leads; no rhythmic evolution, no attenuation, no postictal slowing.

eeg.impression: This is a NORMAL video-EEG. One habitual event was recorded (staring with eyelid fluttering, lasting 1 min 40 s) without ictal EEG change before, during or after the event; the posterior dominant rhythm persisted during the event. No interictal epileptiform discharges. No electrographic seizures.

results.finding: Diagnosis of functional neurological disorder rests on positive clinical features such as the Hoover sign, tremor entrainment and functional seizure semiology, not on the exclusion of other disease; treatment combines explanation, physiotherapy and psychological therapy.
results.source: Espay AJ et al. JAMA Neurol 2018;75:1132-1141

results.finding: Motor signs such as the Hoover sign, hip abductor sign, drift without pronation and dragging gait have high specificity; sensory signs such as midline splitting have low specificity.
results.source: Daum C et al. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2014;85:180-190

results.finding: Defines levels of certainty for psychogenic nonepileptic seizures; the documented level requires a typical event recorded on video-EEG without ictal EEG change.
results.source: LaFrance WC Jr et al. Epilepsia 2013;54:2005-2018

results.finding: For functional seizures: assess for co-occurring epilepsy and psychiatric disorders, taper antiseizure medication without another indication, avoid benzodiazepines, and offer psychological therapy, which is possibly effective.
CBT added to standardised medical care did not reduce dissociative seizure frequency at 12 months; several secondary outcomes favoured CBT.
results.source: Goldstein LH et al. Lancet Psychiatry 2020;7:491-505

results.finding: Specialist physiotherapy for functional motor disorder was not superior to community neurological physiotherapy on physical function at 12 months; several secondary outcomes favoured it.
results.source: Nielsen G et al. Lancet Neurol 2024;23:675-686

results.finding: About 4% of patients diagnosed with conversion symptoms since 1970 later received another diagnosis.

functional neurological disorder diagnos.summary: Guideline and trial evidence supports a positive clinical diagnosis of functional neurological disorder, video-EEG confirmation of functional seizures, tapering of unneeded antiseizure drugs and benzodiazepines, and physiotherapy and psychological treatment whose trial effects on primary outcomes were modest.

additional_observations: Technique: sagittal T1, axial T2, axial FLAIR, DWI with ADC, SWI; no contrast administered
No restricted diffusion in any vascular territory
No hemorrhage, mass or cortical signal abnormality
mri.impression: Normal non-contrast brain MRI. No acute infarct, white matter lesion, mass or hemorrhage.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Clear positive signs of functional left-sided weakness and tremor and typical staring events, with two prompts to over-investigate (migraine-stroke concern, family history of epilepsy); the work-up is the examination and one non-contrast MRI, with a video-EEG capture to confirm the events if needed.
metadata.notes: Straightforward FND with PNES and functional left hemisensorimotor syndrome. PTSD with identified precipitants.
metadata.revision_reason: October 2026 review round: criteria rebuilt to the pack tiers (exam required, MRI recommended), non-contrast MRI, canonical literature and medication outputs, case-specific differential, evidence and assessment. Close-out 24 Oct 2026: video-EEG optional and red-flag tests recommended, per the July 2026 agreement with the physicians that the examination is the only required diagnostic act.

patient.chief_complaint: Acute left-sided weakness and tremor, episodes of staring

medications.frequency: as needed for migraine, max 2 doses/day

past_medical_history: History of sexual abuse in adolescence

social_history.recent_stressor: Witnessed coworker's traumatic injury at work 6 weeks ago; also anniversary of abuse

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. G is a 34-year-old customer service representative who presented via emergency department with acute-onset left arm and leg weakness and left hand tremor developing over 24 hours. She also reports three episodes of staring spells with unresponsiveness over the past week, each lasting approximately 1-2 minutes. She has a history of migraine and was initially concerned she was having a prolonged aura or a migraine-related stroke. Her coworker described today's episode as staring blankly with fluttering eyelids, followed by immediate return to normal consciousness with no confusion afterward. On further history, she reports that she witnessed a traumatic work injury to a close coworker 6 weeks ago where the coworker was struck by machinery. She has been having nightmares and flashbacks since the event. Additionally, the current month marks the anniversary of adolescent sexual abuse she experienced, which has been weighing on her. Her maternal aunt had childhood epilepsy that later resolved, and this worries her. She denies headache, visual changes, dysarthria, or dysphagia. Her fluoxetine dose has been unchanged for 8 months. She reports no prior neurological presentations, though she did have one episode of unexplained right leg weakness during a particularly stressful period 3 years ago that her PCP attributed to anxiety.

neurological_exam.additional: Left hand tremor that entrains to the frequency of external tapping when asked to mimic the examiner's rhythm.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose normal bilaterally. Heel-shin normal on the right; not assessable on the left because of the weakness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. Pupils equal and reactive. No nystagmus.
neurological_exam.gait: Drags the left leg behind with the foot on the floor, holding on to furniture; walked normally out of the bathroom when unaware of being observed.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Calm demeanor but reports feeling dissociated.
neurological_exam.motor: Left arm 1-2/5 on formal testing; with arms outstretched and eyes closed the left arm drifts down without pronation. Hoover sign positive on the left: left hip extension is weak on direct testing but returns to full strength, felt under the left heel, during contralateral right hip flexion against resistance. Left hand tremor that stops when she taps a rhythm with the right hand. Right side 5/5.
neurological_exam.sensory: Left hemisensory loss to face, arm, leg without following anatomical nerve distributions. Loss does not comply with dermatomal pattern.
